Q: Is it possible to make a Test Method generic while using MSTest as test framework? A:

I haven't tested this myself yet, but in march of 2025, MSTest 3.8 released and they reportedly added support for generic test methods: https://devblogs.microsoft.com/dotnet/mstest-3-8-highlights/

Better data-driven tests: Parameterized generic test methods are now supported.

This is also mentioned on their learn page for data driven testing: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/core/testing/unit-testing-mstest-writing-tests-data-driven#generic-test-methods

Starting with MSTest v3.8, a TestMethod can have type parameters. The framework infers type arguments from DataRow or DynamicData values:

[TestMethod]
[DataRow(42)]
[DataRow("alpha")]
public void Value_RoundTrips<T>(T value)
{
    Assert.AreEqual(value, value);
}

Q: How to make this stream gatherer threadsafe? A:

Is my understanding correct or is the stream framework internally synchronizes access to the state objects while performing combiner and finisher operations?

This is closest to the truth. Explicit synchronization isn't exactly how it works, but those processing objects are not expected to be thread-safe.

Q: Getting "Size tap targets appropriately" warning on an element which is not tappable at all A:

The issue has been resolved. The click event was on the parent element and was affecting the children too. Altering the design and detaching the click-able areas in such a way that they are independent was the solution that worked for me.

Q: How is std::vector able to be constexpr without constexpr std::uninitialized_copy? A:

std::vector doesn't use std::uninitialized_copy. It calls std::allocator_traits::construct to perform copy construction. The latter defaults to calling std::construct_at, which is handled specially during constant evaluation ([expr.const]/6).

In practice, compilers treat std::construct_at specially, so that it can use placement new during constant evaluation.

  • MSVC uses a secret attribute to define the placement operator new and to call it inside std::construct_at. (Well, it's not that secret.)
  • Clang permits placement new during constant evaluation when the enclosing function is within namespace std.
  • GCC and EDG permit placement new when the enclosing function template is named std::construct_at.
